title: Zero downtime deploy on a single server with systemd
when: One server runs the app under systemd and the user wants to ship a new version without dropping requests, with an instant way back.
prompt:
Goal: Versioned release folders, an atomic symlink switch and two instances, so one serves while the other restarts.
Steps:
1. Layout: /srv/app/releases/20261017-1530/ per release, /srv/app/shared/ for .env and uploads, /srv/app/current pointing at the live one.
2. Template unit app@.service: WorkingDirectory=/srv/app/current, ExecStart=/usr/bin/node server.mjs, Environment=PORT=%i; run app@3001 and app@3002.
3. The proxy balances both ports and retries the other upstream on connection errors.
4. deploy.sh copies the build into a new release folder, installs from the lockfile there, links shared files and smoke starts it on a spare port.
5. Atomic switch: ln -s releases/NEW /srv/app/current.tmp && mv -T /srv/app/current.tmp /srv/app/current.
6. systemctl restart app@3001, wait for /readyz 200, then restart app@3002.
7. Keep 5 releases; rollback is the same switch to the previous folder plus both restarts.
8. The app drains in flight requests on SIGTERM; TimeoutStopSec=20.
Quality bar:
- A request loop during deploy sees no failures.
- Rollback takes under a minute.
- Schema changes stay compatible with the previous release.
Pitfalls:
- ln -sfn over the live link, which deletes it for a moment.
- Restarting both instances at once.
- Installing dependencies inside the live folder.
Verify:
- [ ] Template unit takes the port from %i.
- [ ] The switch uses mv -T.
- [ ] Each restart waits for readiness.
- [ ] Last 5 releases kept.
Output: deploy/app@.service, deploy/deploy.sh and a Deploy section in README.md.

examples.input: deploy without downtime on my single vps
examples.output: releases/ folders, current symlink swapped with mv -T, app@3001 and app@3002 restarted one by one after /readyz, deploy.sh keeping 5 releases
